entries.title: Proverbs 17:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: False lips - To false accusations and calumnies, which give him occasion and encouragement to do mischief.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Excellent speech - Discourse of high and excellent things.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A precious stone - Pleasant and acceptable; and withal dazzles his eyes. Whithersoever - To whomsoever it is presented. But this, as also many of her proverbs, are to be understood of most men, not of all.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Covereth - That conceals as far as he may, other mens faults.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rebellion - Against God. Messenger - Or, a cruel angel, the angel of death, the devil, or some bloody men employed by God to avenge his quarrel.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Folly - In the heat of his lust or passion.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Letteth out - By cutting the bank of a river. Leave off - Avoid the occasions, and prevent the beginning of contention.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A price - Opportunities and abilities of getting it. No heart - Neither discretion to discern the worth of wisdom, nor any sincere desire to get it.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Was born - Was sent into the world for this, that he might comfort and relieve his brother in adversity.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Friend - Debtor, for whom being his friend, he becomes surety.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No good - Shall not get that advantage which he expects.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Doth good - Even to the body; it contributes much to bodily health and vigour. Drieth - Wastes the marrow of the bones, and the moisture and strength of the body.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In the face - His wisdom appears even in his looks. The eyes - Minding most, those things which are remotest from him, and least concern him.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To strike - Nor to smite magistrates, either with the hand or tongue, for the execution of justice.
